title: HMW Bacterial DNA Extraction Using NEB Monarch® HMW DNA Extraction Kit
author: Jae Hee Jang
materials: NEB Monarch® HMW DNA Extraction Kit

steps.title: Pellet bacterial cells
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the bacterial suspension in a Monarch Pestle Tube (or 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube if unavailable) at 16 000 × g for 1 min (00:01:00). Use 1 × 10⁹–5 × 10⁹ cells for E. coli (≈1 mL overnight culture or equivalent plate scrape). Adjust starting amount upward if DNA yield is low, downward if lysate remains cloudy.

steps.title: Prepare lysozyme solution
steps.instruction: Suspend chicken lysozyme (25 mg/mL) by adding 0.005 g to 200 µL nuclease‑free water; this prepares enough for up to 20 samples. Store the aliquot at –20 °C and avoid repeated freeze‑thaw cycles.

steps.title: Prepare MetaPolyzyme solution
steps.instruction: Resuspend a new tube of MetaPolyzyme Multilytic Enzyme Mix in PBS (pH 7.5), aliquot 200 µL per tube (5 aliquots per tube), and store at –20 °C for future use.

steps.title: Lyse gram‑negative bacteria
steps.instruction: Resuspend the pellet in 300 µL cold PBS (use 150 µL for Low Input). Add 10 µL prepared lysozyme, vortex briefly, then add 300 µL (150 µL Low Input) HMW gDNA Tissue Lysis Buffer. Mix by inverting 5–10 times and incubate at 37 °C in a thermal mixer with agitation at 1000 rpm for at least 2 h (02:00:00). For most applications use 1400–2000 rpm; for maximal fragment size use 500 rpm. Continue until lysate is clear (cloudy lysate may be acceptable for Salmonella/E. coli).

steps.title: Lyse gram‑positive bacteria
steps.instruction: Resuspend the pellet in 150 µL cold PBS, add 10 µL MetaPolyzyme, invert 5–10 times, and incubate at 37 °C without agitation for at least 2 h (preferably up to 24 h). Add an additional 150 µL cold PBS, invert 5–10 times, then add 300 µL (150 µL Low Input) HMW gDNA Tissue Lysis Buffer and invert 5–10 times.

steps.title: Raise temperature to 56 °C
steps.instruction: After the lysozyme (or MetaPolyzyme) incubation, increase the thermal mixer block temperature to 56 °C.

steps.title: Add Proteinase K and incubate
steps.instruction: Add 20 µL Proteinase K (10 µL for Low Input) and invert 10–20 times. Incubate at 56 °C for 30 min (00:30:00) in a thermal mixer at 1000 rpm (use 1400–2000 rpm for 50–250 kb fragments; lower speed for Mb‑range). If the sample remains cloudy after this step, lysis has failed.

steps.title: Add RNase A and incubate
steps.instruction: Add 10 µL RNase A (5 µL Low Input) and invert 5–10 times. Incubate for 10 min (00:10:00) at 56 °C with the same agitation speed used in the previous step.

steps.title: Add Protein Separation Solution
steps.instruction: Add 300 µL Protein Separation Solution (150 µL Low Input) and mix by inverting for 1 min (00:01:00). A vertical rotating mixer at 20 rpm may be used as an alternative.

steps.title: Phase‑separation centrifugation
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the mixture at 16 000 × g for 10 min (00:10:00). During centrifugation, prepare the plastics required for Part 2 (see next step). After spin, a clear upper DNA phase and a lower protein phase will be visible; a white precipitate may also be present. If phase separation is incomplete, extend centrifugation 10–20 min.

steps.title: Prepare sample plastics
steps.instruction: For each sample gather: a Monarch Collection Tube II, a Monarch Bead Retainer (to be placed in the collection tube), two Monarch 2 mL tubes (one for phase separation, one for elution), and a 1.5 mL low‑bind microfuge tube (DNA not supplied). Label all tubes appropriately.

steps.title: Transfer upper DNA phase
steps.instruction: Using a 200 µL wide‑bore tip, transfer the clear upper phase (≈800 µL; ≈400 µL Low Input) to a labeled Monarch 2 mL tube. Avoid the protein layer; if no lower protein phase is visible, leave ~30 µL behind. If total volume is <700 µL (<350 µL Low Input), note that the isopropanol volume in Step 13 must be adjusted to 0.7 × sample volume.

steps.title: Prepare isopropanol aliquot
steps.instruction: Aliquot 550 µL isopropanol per sample (prepare ~1 mL extra as overage). For Low Input use 275 µL, or use 0.7 × sample volume if the transferred volume is <700 µL.

steps.title: Add DNA Capture Beads
steps.instruction: Using a clean inoculating loop, add 2 DNA Capture Beads to each Monarch 2 mL tube containing the transferred phase. Flip the loop upside‑down to release the beads; the same loop may be reused if it has not contacted any sample.

steps.title: Bind DNA with isopropanol
steps.instruction: Add the appropriate volume of isopropanol (550 µL, 275 µL Low Input, or 0.7 × sample volume), close the cap, and invert the tube slowly and gently by hand for 5 min (minimum). Perform ~25–30 full inversions (each ~5–6 s) until the solution is no longer viscous and DNA is visibly bound to the beads. Flick the tube if beads stick to the bottom.

steps.title: Remove supernatant
steps.instruction: Using a P1000 pipette, carefully remove and discard the liquid without disturbing the bead‑DNA complex. Angle the tube so beads remain at the bottom; keep the tube nearly horizontal at the end. Proceed quickly to the next buffer to avoid drying the beads.

steps.title: First gDNA wash
steps.instruction: Add 500 µL gDNA Wash Buffer, close the cap, and invert 2–3 times. Then remove the wash buffer as described in the previous step. The gDNA complex will condense around the beads.

steps.title: Second gDNA wash
steps.instruction: Repeat the addition of 500 µL gDNA Wash Buffer, invert 2–3 times, and remove the buffer with a P1000 pipette. Complete removal of all wash buffer is not required at this stage.

steps.title: Transfer beads to collection tube
steps.instruction: Place a labeled Bead Retainer into a Monarch Collection Tube II, pour the beads from the 2 mL tube into the retainer, close the cap, and discard the used 2 mL tube. Close the cap of the Bead Retainer after each transfer when handling multiple samples.

steps.title: Pulse‑spin to remove residual buffer
steps.instruction: Pulse‑spin (≤1 s) the collection tube in a benchtop minicentrifuge to expel any remaining wash buffer from the beads.

steps.title: Move beads to new 2 mL tube
steps.instruction: Separate the Bead Retainer from the collection tube, pour the beads into a new labeled Monarch 2 mL tube, and insert the used Bead Retainer into a labeled 1.5 mL low‑bind microfuge tube for later elution. Discard the empty collection tube.

steps.title: Elute DNA from beads
steps.instruction: Add 100 µL Elution Buffer II (50 µL may be used if desired) directly onto the beads, close the cap, and incubate for at least 5 min (00:05:00) at 56 °C in a thermal mixer at 300 rpm. Halfway through, tilt the tube almost horizontally and gently shake to keep beads suspended. If using <100 µL, shake several times during incubation.

steps.title: Collect eluate in low‑bind tube
steps.instruction: Insert the Bead Retainer into the 1.5 mL low‑bind tube, pour the eluate (and beads) into the retainer, and close the cap. If any eluate remains in the 2 mL tube, briefly spin and transfer the remainder.

steps.title: Separate eluate from beads
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the 1.5 mL tube at 12 000 × g for 30 s (00:00:30) to pellet the beads. Discard the beads and retainer, retaining the clear eluate.

steps.title: Homogenize DNA solution
steps.instruction: Pipette the eluate up and down 5–10 times with a wide‑bore tip to ensure homogeneous dissolution and to disperse any visible aggregates.

steps.title: Post‑elution incubation
steps.instruction: Incubate the DNA solution as needed: 1 h at 37 °C (01:00:00), overnight at room temperature, or longer at 4 °C.

steps.title: Store and quantify DNA
steps.instruction: Store the purified DNA at 4 °C for short‑term use. Before analysis, pipette up and down 5–10 times again. Quantify using 2 µL of DNA with the Qubit™ dsDNA BR Assay Kit for higher accuracy.

steps.title: Optional sample storage
steps.instruction: If extraction is not performed the same day, store pelleted cells at –20 °C for up to 1 month (avoid repeated freeze‑thaw). Lysed samples may be kept at 4 °C overnight.
